learningObjectives.title: Control: propaganda, terror and the police state
Life for young people, women and workers

questions.q: On what date did the Reichstag Fire take place?
questions.explain: The Reichstag building was set alight on 27 February 1933, giving Hitler a pretext to suspend civil rights.

questions.q: In which year was the Enabling Act passed?
questions.explain: The Enabling Act was passed on 24 March 1933, allowing Hitler to rule by decree.

questions.q: On what date did the Night of the Long Knives take place?
questions.explain: The purge of the SA leadership and other opponents occurred on 30 June 1934.

questions.q: Who was the Nazi Minister of Propaganda?
questions.explain: Joseph Goebbels headed the Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda, controlling all forms of media.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the SS?
questions.explain: Heinrich Himmler led the SS, which ran the police state, concentration camps and later the Holocaust.

questions.q: What was the name of the Nazi youth organisation for girls?
questions.explain: The League of German Maidens (Bund Deutscher Maedel) prepared girls for their future roles as wives and mothers.

questions.q: After trade unions were banned in 1933, which organisation did workers have to join?
questions.explain: The German Labour Front (DAF), led by Robert Ley, replaced the banned trade unions.

questions.q: In which year were the Nuremberg Laws introduced?
questions.explain: The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 stripped Jews of German citizenship and banned marriage between Jews and non-Jews.

questions.q: Why was the Enabling Act so significant for Hitler?
options: It gave Hitler the power to make laws without the approval of the Reichstag
It made Hitler President of Germany
It banned all other political parties immediately
questions.explain: The Enabling Act let Hitler pass laws for four years without the Reichstag, effectively ending democracy.

questions.q: How did the Night of the Long Knives strengthen Hitler's position?
options: It abolished the office of President
It removed the threat from the SA and won the support of the army
questions.explain: Eliminating Roehm and the SA leadership reassured the army, which soon swore a personal oath of loyalty to Hitler.

questions.q: What was a key aim of Nazi propaganda?
options: To encourage open debate of political ideas
To build support for the Nazis and glorify Hitler
To promote women in the workplace
questions.explain: Propaganda aimed to win loyalty to the regime and create a cult of the Fuehrer around Hitler.

questions.q: What was the role of the Gestapo in Nazi Germany?
options: The secret state police who arrested opponents of the regime
questions.explain: The Gestapo were the secret police who used informers to arrest and imprison suspected opponents, often without trial.

questions.q: The slogan 'Kinder, Kueche, Kirche' summed up the Nazi view that a woman's proper role was concerned with:
questions.explain: The slogan meant 'children, kitchen, church', reflecting the Nazi belief that women belonged in the home.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of the 'Strength Through Joy' (KdF) programme?
options: To train boys for military service
To provide cheap holidays and leisure activities for workers
To organise the invasion of Poland
questions.explain: Strength Through Joy offered subsidised leisure and holidays to keep workers content and loyal to the regime.

questions.q: What does Kristallnacht (November 1938) refer to?
options: An organised attack on Jewish homes, businesses and synagogues
The opening of the first concentration camp
questions.explain: Kristallnacht, the 'Night of Broken Glass', saw Jewish property and synagogues attacked and thousands of Jews arrested.

questions.q: What was the purpose of the Wannsee Conference of 1942?
options: To plan the invasion of Poland
To organise the 'Final Solution' to the 'Jewish question'
To sign a treaty with the Soviet Union
questions.explain: At Wannsee, Nazi leaders coordinated the systematic mass murder of Europe's Jews in extermination camps.

questions.q: A German boy in 1938 spends his weekends camping, marching and doing physical training in a Nazi organisation. Which organisation does he most likely belong to?
questions.explain: The Hitler Youth used camping, marching and fitness to build loyalty and prepare boys for military service.

questions.q: After 1935, a Jewish person in Germany finds they can no longer be a German citizen or marry a non-Jew. This is a direct result of the:
questions.explain: The Nuremberg Laws removed Jewish citizenship and outlawed marriage between Jews and other Germans.

questions.q: In 1937 a factory worker is reported by a neighbour for criticising Hitler and is arrested without trial. This best illustrates the Nazi use of:
questions.explain: Arrests based on informers and without trial were central to the atmosphere of fear in the Nazi police state.

questions.q: In August 1934, following the death of President Hindenburg, Hitler combined the roles of Chancellor and President and adopted which title?
questions.explain: On Hindenburg's death Hitler merged the offices of Chancellor and President and took the title Fuehrer, becoming sole leader.
